_note: Original advanced concept questions for linked lists.

questions.title: Node parts
questions.code:
Node sketch:
[value | next]

Example:
[10 | next] -> [20 | null]
questions.prompt: What two things does a basic linked-list node store?
choices: A value and a next link
A sorted array and a queue
questions.explanation: A node stores data and a link to the next node.

questions.title: Head pointer
questions.prompt: What does the head of a linked list refer to?
questions.explanation: Traversal starts at the head, then follows next links.

questions.title: Insert after a node
questions.prompt: Arrange the safe steps to insert `newNode` after `current`.
lines: Continue traversal from the node you need next.
questions.explanation: The new node must point to the old next node before current.next is overwritten.

questions.title: Delete after current
questions.prompt: To remove the node after `current`, which link usually changes?
questions.explanation: Deleting a node means changing a link so the list skips that node.

questions.title: Lost link
questions.prompt: Why is `current.next = newNode` before `newNode.next = current.next` a bug?
choices: It loses the old next node.
questions.explanation: Once current.next is overwritten, the old next node may no longer be reachable.

questions.title: Traversal stop
questions.prompt: When does a basic linked-list traversal stop?
choices: When the current node becomes null/None
questions.explanation: A null/None link means there is no next node to visit. Traversal keeps following next links until that missing link tells the loop it has moved past the final real node.

questions.title: No direct index
questions.code:
Array:
items[10]

Linked list:
head -> node -> node -> ...
questions.prompt: Why is finding the 10th item different in a linked list than in an array?
choices: You must follow links one by one.
The list automatically jumps by index.
A linked list cannot store numbers.
questions.explanation: A linked list does not provide direct index access; you move node by node.

questions.title: Cycle risk
questions.prompt: What can happen if a linked-list node accidentally points back to an earlier node?
questions.explanation: A backward link can create a cycle, so traversal may never reach null/None.
